subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel Little Women. Jo, a young aspiring writer, has committed to improving her craft through disciplined practice.

Jo believed that mastering the art of writing required nothing less than complete dedication, and she had devised a plan to write something every single day for an entire year. She was composing a different type of piece each week in methodical rotation and never allowing herself to skip the challenging forms. She remembered starting with sonnets in January. She had been writing daily for many months now and had already completed weeks of sonnets and short stories, character sketches and descriptive essays. For all her ambition, she had to acknowledge that some of the poetry weeks had been particularly difficult. But Jo was a writer.

©1868 by Louisa May Alcott
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To illustrate Jo's enjoyment of an unusual writing style
choices.B: To explain why Jo prefers writing over other artistic pursuits
choices.C: To portray Jo's determination to meet a goal
choices.D: To describe a story that Jo greatly admires

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately describes the main purpose of the text, which is to portray Jo's determination to reach her goal of mastering writing through daily practice. The text indicates that to achieve this aim, Jo works systematically and persistently: she writes something every day in methodical rotation and devotes significant time and effort to the project, maintaining her practice over many months. The text then suggests that even though she encounters difficulties ("some of the poetry weeks had been particularly difficult") and challenging forms that she doesn't skip, she doesn't give up because she thinks of herself as "a writer." These details show Jo's resolve.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. Although the text mentions several writing forms (sonnets and short stories, character sketches and descriptive essays) that Jo has practiced, it doesn't indicate that any of these forms are unusual or that she especially enjoyed writing in one of these forms in particular. If anything, the text suggests that she may have found some of these forms to be difficult, saying that she never skips the "challenging forms" and that some of the poetry weeks were "particularly difficult," meaning they were hard to complete.
